fatal_errors: The asserted directional FCC-to-BCC transition and Ti-driven HCP precipitation are not established by the target, which reports a stable mixed 83% FCC/17% BCC structure without an HCP result.
Low-load Vickers testing alone cannot isolate grain-boundary strengthening from precipitation hardening; matched grain-size and phase-fraction controls are required.
explanation: The hypothesis correctly identifies the central HEBM-plus-SPS strategy, approximately 6 h milling, 1000°C sintering, strain/grain refinement, densification, VEC/atomic-size effects, and improvement over porous cast material. It omits most critical processing conditions, including 400 rpm, 20:1 ball-to-powder ratio, argon milling, vacuum SPS, 50°C/min heating, and the 10 min hold. It also fails to predict the quantitative phase fraction, sub-48 nm grain size, density, 675 Hv hardness, or compressive properties. Mechanistically, it captures grain-boundary strengthening but underrepresents dislocation and solid-solution strengthening and overstates an unsupported FCC-to-BCC direction and HCP pathway. The proposed temperature comparison is useful, but the boundary omits excessive milling and density saturation, while the falsification design needs phase/grain-matched controls and the target 0.05 kN, 15 s hardness protocol. No supporting evidence is cited.
